title: Tartuffe at New York Theatre Workshop #tartuffe #nytw #lucashnath #th...
transcript: The second Tartuffe of this off-Broadway season just started previews at New York Theatre Workshop with an unbelievably stacked cast. Matthew Broderick is in the lead role accompanied by folks like Francis Jue, Amber Gray, and Bianca Del Rio, to name a few, so the bar is high. My experience was a bit of a mixed bag, but I did attend the second preview, which had its share of small line mishaps and pacing hiccups, causing the spark to not always be there. Still, I feel pretty confident that the show is going to be in a solid place in due time. For one, the performances are in good hands — everyone in this cast has such a distinct presence which I think works really well for this campy production. Although it does sometimes feel like everyone's in a slightly different version of the world, it allows them to play to their specific comedic strengths. The adaptation by Lucas Hnath is funny and unexpected — it's in verse, but it blends high brow vocabulary with blunt and vulgar language. I'm not quite sure what to make of the direction — the scene work is fine but the overall concept is a mystery to me. There's some stuff with tennis going on during the scene transitions and in the set design that I honestly do not understand, so I'm hoping some clarity emerges there. Overall, definitely a work in progress, but I'm leaning positive and I certainly had an enjoyable second preview experience. With that, another program for my collection.
